title: The 5-3-1 Rule and Social Fitness
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Drawing on Harvard's decades-long adult-development study and author Kasley Killam's work, this article translates relationship quality into a concrete weekly practice for "social fitness." It reports that the strongest predictor of health and happiness across the Harvard study's 724 participants was the quality and strength of personal relationships, not wealth or career success. Killam's 5-3-1 rule operationalizes this: connect with five different people weekly, nurture three close relationships daily, and spend at least one hour a day in quality conversation. The piece frames social wellness as a discipline requiring the same regularity as physical fitness, arguing that consistent contact, not occasional deep conversation, is what sustains well-being.
points: The 80-plus-year Harvard adult-development study found relationship quality is the strongest predictor of health and happiness, ahead of other life factors.
Kasley Killam's 5-3-1 rule prescribes five varied weekly connections, three daily check-ins with close friends, and one hour of daily quality conversation.
Diversifying the "five" weekly contacts, mixing new and old relationships, is specifically called out as improving well-being outcomes.
Social wellness requires daily discipline, not just periodic deep conversations reserved for weekends or special occasions.
quotes: In the longest-known examination of adult development, Harvard University has tracked the lives of 724 people since 1938.
By far the strongest predictor of health and happiness was the quality and strengths of a person’s relationships.
5: Spend time with five different people each week. These could be neighbors, colleagues, old friends, or new acquaintances.
3: Nurture three close relationships every day. These are the friends you depend upon for support and enjoyment.
1: Strive for one hour of quality interaction each day. Conversation is how relationships get done.
